title: Uchrony: the world at your table
question: I’m shaping a map-first simulation workspace. Choose a direction or leave a steer while I build the simulation engine.

options.label: The cabinet map table
options.thesis: A living political map occupies the table; state dossiers and decisions sit within reach.
options.viewport: A broad interactive atlas, a narrow chronicle on the left, and an inspectable state dossier on the right; time controls below.
options.risk: Dense information needs strong hierarchy on smaller screens.

raised.raise: Map layers change the whole field consistently, with an explicit live legend.
One selected place remains the anchor across every panel.
Economy and policy show compact comparable rows, not scattered cards.
Fixed time-series scales make changes legible.
One map owns the main visual field.

options.label: The survey atlas
options.thesis: A bright cartographic sheet with compact instruments and an open data drawer.
options.viewport: A full map with floating map tools and a pale bottom ledger.
options.risk: A familiar strategy-game arrangement, effective but less distinctive.

options.label: The night atlas
options.thesis: A dark observation chart makes cities and goods movement the brightest objects.
options.viewport: A night map dominated by settlement lights and routes, with faint territory colors.
options.case: Strong for observing flows; weaker at reading political territory.
options.risk: National borders and terrain can become too quiet.

options.label: Type specimen
options.thesis: One parameter reshapes a field of observations.
options.viewport: A large parameter slider over comparative samples.
options.case: Less familiar to map-simulation users and less clear for spatial geography.

options.label: Airport wayfinding
options.thesis: Every decision retains a clearly signed destination.
options.viewport: Large directions above a compact route map.
options.case: Journey guidance does not fit simultaneous world observation.

options.label: Dense reference desk
options.thesis: A packed grid exposes all the live information.
options.viewport: Many small tables surround a small map.
options.case: Strong data access but weaker geographical focus and identification.

options.label: Seasonal folio
options.thesis: Registered frames reveal change over time.
options.viewport: Repeated maps show distinct historical stages.
options.case: Better for reviewing history than controlling a live simulation.

options.label: Records catalog
options.thesis: A single plot dominates an indexed world.
options.case: Coded controls weaken policy clarity and audience familiarity.
options.kept: One dominant map, restrained surrounding chrome.

canonCard.label: Conventional grand strategy
canonCard.thesis: Familiar strategy-game panels around a political map.
canonCard.viewport: Top resource bar, full map, side detail panels.
